# Rust-Crate-Dreams

This repository is an archive of grounded ideas and product plans for ideal yet missing Rust crates.

Start here, in order:
1. README.md
2. INDEX.md
3. entries/2026-03-25-467.md
4. meta/frontier-failure-envelopes-2026-03-25.md
5. meta/epic-crate-falsification-counterexample-and-failure-envelope-doctrine-2026-03-25.md
6. meta/top-lane-falsification-plans-2026-03-25.md
7. failure-envelopes.json
8. assurance-cases.json
9. delta-programs.json
10. renewal-programs.json

19. meta/archive-memory-anchor-2026-03-22.md

Use latest-first discipline:
- prefer the newest entry and the newest meta files it names;
- do not rerank the frontier without reading the latest source-basis note;
- distinguish facts, inferences, and open questions explicitly;
- do not reopen giant umbrella sectors unless they beat the current control-plane frontier on receiver value and bounded first release;
- do not call a crate "worthy" unless you can name its acceptance packet family, support ceiling, recheck triggers, refusal boundary, package topology, and cheap change-handling story;
- do not invent a new packet format without naming its schema/version policy, profile semantics, verifier behavior, and import/export route;
- do not say a crate is "supported" without naming the support dimension, evidence tier, matrix/profile scope, and basis;
- do not call a crate decision-ready unless you can name the policy pack, verdict vocabulary, override path, and recheck triggers;
- do not imply `1.0` maturity unless packet semantics and handoff semantics are both stable;
- do not call a crate review-ready unless you can name the review packet, decisive evidence slice, signoff ledger, active overrides, and reapproval plan;
- do not call a crate sustainably maintainable unless you can name the renewal unit, freshness budget, cheapest honest rerun slice, owner/escalation path, and retirement/supersession rule;
- do not call a crate cheaply updatable unless you can name the change class, carry-forward rule, minimum rerun slice, confidence-reset rule, and supersession diff semantics;
- do not call a crate assurance-ready unless you can name the claim family, decisive witnesses, warrant vocabulary, challenge/non-claim surface, and inheritance or supersession rule;
- do not call a crate falsification-ready unless you can name the failing scenario, decisive counterexample, degraded surviving claim, withdrawn guarantee, and repair or replay slice;
- do not force a worthy contribution into one package when CLI, library, schema, and adapter surfaces have different stability needs;
- do not split packages unless the split improves receiver clarity or isolates substrate churn.

What this archive tends to prefer:
- receiver-facing control-plane crates;
- evidence, support, parity, transition, handoff, review-memory, renewal, delta-handling, and falsification infrastructure;
- narrow honest first releases over big umbrella fantasies.
